answer: A farm that floods the queue early therefore gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. Because the cedar ordering is published with the pulse batch, the forge audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 49% of the queue is processed in arrival order. A 142 account operation therefore ties up 26 million dollars of idle capital. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
